policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in A (pick up the container), with the point on the first entry of target_containers computed from the demonstration at that same step. Rules at any decision step: (1) If the scene shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open), it is holding a container: choose B (put down the container). (2) If the fingers are fully open (about 100%) and put_down_count is less than the number of entries in target_containers, choose A and point at the container whose current listed position is nearest to target_containers[put_down_count + 1] (1-based: the first entry when put_down_count is 0, the second when it is 1); write the point as that container's listed position. (3) If the fingers are fully open and put_down_count equals the number of entries, every named container has been handled; choose A and point at the last entry of target_containers again (harmless repeat). If a situation matches none of these rules (e.g. gripper state unclear), pick the rule whose gripper description is closest: partly closed fingers mean B, open fingers mean A on the next unhandled target.

fields.name: target_containers
fields.description: Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first frame listing containers, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube; the positions listed in that frame are the slots; label the named container by its slot; (3) walk the frames after the first container frame in order and keep a running slot assignment. A SHUFFLE is a maximal run of consecutive frames in which two containers are off their slots (well over 10 pixels); it ENDS at the first later frame where all containers are again at slots. At that ending frame, swap the slots of the two containers whose slots were empty during the run. Keep walking: if a later frame again shows two containers off their slots, that is a NEW shuffle, even if it is the same two slots as before, and it swaps them again when it ends. Before computing the answer, write out the list of shuffles in order (e.g. 'shuffle 1: slots P and Q, frames 80-96, ends 112; shuffle 2: slots P and Q, frames 128-144, ends 160'). Two shuffles of the same pair put them back where they started; three leave them swapped. Shuffles of other pairs do not change the named container's slot; (4) never assume a container returns to its own starting slot, and never take the container resting nearest the cube's original position in the last frame; the entry is the named container's slot after every swap, written with that slot's coordinates as listed in the last demonstration frame. Worked example: cube at [70, 119]; containers first rest at [66, 120], [84, 109], [93, 163], [119, 145]; the cube's container is [66, 120]; later frames show [66, 120] and [84, 109] both off their slots for three frames, then all back; those two swapped, so the cube's container is now the one at [84, 110] in the last frame; entry [84, 110]. Second worked example (two shuffles of one pair): cube at [103, 138]; containers first rest at [91, 78], [100, 139], [104, 178]; the cube's container is at slot [100, 139]; frames 80 and 96 show the [100, 139] and [104, 178] containers off their slots, frame 112 shows all at slots (shuffle 1: those two swap, cube's container now at slot [104, 178]); frames 128 and 144 again show the same two slots empty, frame 160 shows all at slots (shuffle 2: they swap back, cube's container at slot [100, 139]); last frame lists that slot as [101, 139]; entry [[101, 139]]. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]

fields.name: put_down_count
fields.description: Number of containers picked up and then put down so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. Add one to the carried-in value when the execution steps of the current step show the fingers reopening from about 46% to about 100% after being lowered over a container (a put-down just completed); otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1
